tutorial_questions.question: State the definition of product reliability used in the lecture.
tutorial_questions.expected_answer: The probability that a product will operate within specification for a specified duration under designed operating conditions without failure.

tutorial_questions.question: A switch is rated for 20,000 actuations and used 5 times per day. Estimate rated life in years.
In 100 components using 500-hour bins, 12 fail in one bin. Calculate the PDF estimate.
If 28 of 100 components have failed by 2000 h, calculate CDF and reliability.
At the start of an interval 80 units survive and 8 fail. What is the failure-rate fraction?
Explain PDF, CDF, reliability, and hazard physically.
tutorial_questions.expected_answer: PDF describes failure-time distribution; CDF is fraction/probability failed by time t; reliability is fraction/probability surviving beyond t and equals 1-CDF; hazard is failure tendency among units surviving to that point.

tutorial_questions.question: What do decreasing, constant, and increasing hazards indicate?
tutorial_questions.expected_answer: Decreasing hazard: early-life failures. Constant hazard: normal-life random failures. Increasing hazard: end-of-life/wear-out failures.

tutorial_questions.question: For a Weibull model, interpret beta <1, =1, >1, and eta.
tutorial_questions.expected_answer: Beta is shape: beta<1 early-life, beta=1 constant-hazard normal-life, beta>1 wear-out. Eta is the scale parameter or characteristic-life scale.

tutorial_questions.question: Why is the bathtub curve useful for a system with many components?
tutorial_questions.expected_answer: It separates early-life, normal-life, and wear-out regions, which can involve different mechanisms and may require different fitted distributions or maintenance approaches.

tutorial_questions.question: Components with reliabilities 0.98, 0.95 and 0.99 are required in series. Calculate system reliability.
tutorial_questions.expected_answer: R=0.98×0.95×0.99=0.92169≈0.922. Series reliability is lower than the least reliable component.

tutorial_questions.question: Two redundant components have reliabilities 0.90 and 0.80. Calculate parallel reliability.
Explain series-system warranty reliability versus availability in a redundant system.
tutorial_questions.expected_answer: Warranty/series reliability treats any component failure as requiring service, so all components must remain healthy. Availability considers whether redundancy allows continued operation despite one failed component.

tutorial_questions.question: Distinguish MTTF, MTBF and MTTR.
tutorial_questions.expected_answer: MTTF is mean time to failure for a population/non-repairable item; MTBF is mean operating time between failures for repairable/replaced systems; MTTR is mean time to repair.

tutorial_questions.question: MTBF=900 h and MTTR=100 h. Calculate in-service and downtime rates.
If MTBF=5000 h, calculate the average hazard rate using the course relationship.
A system has element hazard rates 0.0001, 0.0003 and 0.0002 per hour. What is the system average hazard rate?
What cost categories are included in total cost of ownership?
tutorial_questions.expected_answer: Purchase, operating, downtime, service, useful-life, and residual-value costs.

tutorial_questions.question: Why is preventive maintenance particularly relevant for wear-out behaviour?
tutorial_questions.expected_answer: Wear-out has increasing hazard with age, so preventive servicing or replacement before the high-risk region can reduce unexpected failures and downtime.
